attempts.label: DANDI:000576
attempts.paper_title: The relation between neuronal firing, local field potentials and hemodynamic activity in the human amygdala in response to aversive dynamic visual stimuli
attempts.entry_title: iEEG, neurons and BOLD in the human amygdala during aversive videos (Fedele, Tzovara et al. 2020)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Fedele, Tzovara et al. (2020) on dandiset 000576, which holds the bipolar amygdala iEEG of 9 patients (14 amygdalae) and the spike times of 42 units from 5 of them during a block design of aversive and neutral videos. It tests the delta and high gamma responses, the modulation indices and their relation to the seizure onset zone, and the firing of the units. The BOLD time courses and the continuous microwire signals are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Fedele, Tzovara et al. (2020) from dandiset 000576

outcomes.statement: In amygdalae outside the SOZ, delta power (1-4 Hz) is lower during AVERSIVE than during NEUTRAL sequences, and the reduction lasts through the AVERSIVE sequence.
outcomes.quote: In nSOZ amygdalae, DELTA band power was consistently reduced throughout the duration of the AVERSIVE sequence (Fig. 1B)

statistics.test: linear mixed model per time point, cluster-based permutation correction (Fig. 1 legend calls it cluster analysis)

outcomes.notes: The criterion blocks the claim when the readings disagree, and they do; it holds in 6 of the 12 mixed-model readings of the claims file. With the z-score over the whole 26 s trial no reading finds a delta cluster (smallest cluster p 0.88 in all 14 amygdalae, 1.0 in the 7 nSOZ). With z-scoring against the 2 s baseline, AVERSIVE is below NEUTRAL with significant clusters covering 14.3 s of the 24 s block in the nSOZ amygdalae and 15.6 s in all 14. With z-scoring over all trials of the amygdala, 17.1 s in all 14 and none in the nSOZ amygdalae (smallest p 0.072). The block mean of AVERSIVE minus NEUTRAL is negative under every reading (-0.03 to -1.39). The variants agree with the baseline reading (baselinepool 13.3 and 16.8 s, trialsd 7.0 and 16.1 s). The unpaired t-test variant gives the same pattern. The question for the authors is in the findings (methods_unavailable, z-scoring).
deviations: The paper's mixed model Power ~ condition + (1|Patients) is computed in its within-patient form (patient fixed effects), which gives the same condition estimate for this balanced design (8 AVERSIVE and 9 NEUTRAL trials per amygdala); the notebook compares it with statsmodels' MixedLM at four time points (t -2.125 against -2.123 and so on).

Labels are permuted within each patient, the same permutation for both amygdalae of a patient (Methods 4.11, "permuted the labels of neutral and aversive trials across all participants", 500 permutations); the unpaired t-test variant permutes over all trials.
The test is run over the 24 s block (0 to 24 s from onset, Fig. 1 "locked to stimulus onset"); the baseline clip is left out. A choice, stated in the notebook.

Outcomes are judged on the three z-scorings of the claims file (trial, baseline, amygdala). Two variants are shown and enter no count of readings, trialsd (the baseline-corrected envelope divided by its SD in the trial) and baselinepool (the epoch's baseline mean and the SD of the baseline clips pooled over the amygdala's epochs, a stable form of baseline z-scoring). The two other baselines of Methods 4.8 (mean of all epochs, previous epoch) are also run as variants.
Envelopes are filtered per 26 s epoch with 2 s mirror padding, as the epochs are not contiguous in the files, and kept at 10 Hz after the 1 s smoothing (standard choices).

outcomes.statement: High gamma power (above 60 Hz) is higher during AVERSIVE than during NEUTRAL sequences in the first 2 s of the sequence.
outcomes.quote: The HGP was enhanced in response to aversive stimuli during the first 2 s of the AVERSIVE sequence presentation (Fig. 1C, unpaired t-tests, corrected for multiple comparisons using random permutations, p < 0.05)

statistics.test: unpaired t-tests, corrected for multiple comparisons using random permutations (Results); linear mixed model with cluster-based permutation (Methods 4.11)

outcomes.notes: None of the 12 mixed-model readings and none of the 12 unpaired t-test readings of the claims file finds a significant HGP cluster, nor do the two z-scoring variants. The largest mixed-model t in the first 2 s is 3.01 at 0.95 s after onset (baseline z-scoring, nSOZ amygdalae), above the threshold at 13 time points, and its cluster has permutation p 0.062; the smallest cluster p of all mixed-model readings is 0.056. With the HGP band limited to 60-150 or 60-250 Hz (variants of the open upper edge) the only significant HGP clusters are AVERSIVE above NEUTRAL from about 6 to 8 s (p 0.020 and 0.042) and, with baselinepool, 3.1 to 4.7 s, not in the first 2 s. Among the baselines of Methods 4.8 (variants), the previous epoch as baseline with z-scoring over the amygdala gives an HGP cluster from 0.6 to 5.5 s in the nSOZ amygdalae (p 0.002); as blocks alternate, that baseline is always a block of the other condition. With the trialsd variant two more HGP clusters begin in the first 2 s, both in the nSOZ amygdalae, 0.6 to 1.9 s with the mean of all epochs as baseline (p 0.028) and 0.5 to 8.4 s with the previous epoch (p 0.002). These three are the only HGP clusters that begin in the first 2 s, and all use a baseline other than the 1 s clip. Per-amygdala time courses are in the notebook.
deviations: As fig1b-delta-decrease. HGP is a 60 Hz high-pass (the claims file's reading); two band-pass variants are shown and do not decide the outcome.

outcomes.statement: No AVERSIVE against NEUTRAL difference is found in the theta, alpha, beta and gamma (30-60 Hz) bands.
outcomes.quote: Since no effect was observed in the other spectral bands (see Methods 7.8), in the following we focus on DELTA power and HGP
outcomes.notes: The readings of the claims file disagree. Under the z-score over the whole trial no band has a cluster, nor has delta. Under baseline z-scoring the mixed model finds clusters with AVERSIVE below NEUTRAL in alpha in the 7 nSOZ amygdalae (13.3 to 15.9 s, p 0.016) and in theta and alpha in all 14 (p 0.002 to 0.028); under z-scoring over the amygdala all four bands have clusters in all 14 and none in the nSOZ amygdalae. Every reading that shows the delta effect of Fig. 1B (6 of 12) shows a cluster in another band. Of the variants, baselinepool in the nSOZ amygdalae shows the delta effect and no other-band cluster; in all 14 it has theta and alpha clusters.
deviations: Assumed that the paper's pipeline is one under which its own delta result (Fig. 1B) appears, as the paper reports the delta effect and the absence in other bands from the same analysis (Results 2.1, paragraph 1). The outcome is judged on the readings of the claims file that show the delta effect; the trial reading shows no cluster in any band, delta included. The first revision adopted baseline z-scoring alone; the verifier found that the author's own choice, and it is no longer used.

Outcomes are judged on the three z-scorings of the claims file (trial, baseline, amygdala). Two variants are shown and enter no count of readings, trialsd (the baseline-corrected envelope divided by its SD in the trial) and baselinepool (the epoch's baseline mean and the SD of the baseline clips pooled over the amygdala's epochs, a stable form of baseline z-scoring). The two other baselines of Methods 4.8 (mean of all epochs, previous epoch) are also run as variants.
As fig1b-delta-decrease for the test.

outcomes.notes: No reading gives all 28 values within tolerance (at best 4 of 28 among the claims file's z-scorings, z-scoring over the amygdala with fixed windows; 6 with the trialsd variant) or all 28 signs (at best 23 of 28). Where a window reading finds no significant window for an amygdala, its MI is undefined (the first revision set it to 0); a claim is judged on the readings that define every MI it needs.

outcomes.quote: MI and HGP-MI were negatively correlated across all amygdalae
outcomes.notes: Only window (c) defines both MIs. Under it r = -0.30 (p = 0.30), -0.12 (p = 0.69) and -0.12 (p = 0.68) for z-scoring over the trial, against the baseline and over the amygdala; the variants give -0.33 and -0.04. None is within tolerance or has p < 0.05. The printed Table 2 values give r = -0.74 (p = 0.003).

Assumption. Window (c), fixed windows of 0 to 2 s for HGP and 0 to 24 s for delta, is the only window reading that defines the MIs this claim needs, so the outcome rests on it. outcomes.statement: In the left amygdala of Participant 4, the BOLD time course is negatively correlated with DELTA power and positively correlated with HGP over the video sequence.
outcomes.source: Results 2.2, paragraph 2; Figure 2A and 2C; Table 2, amygdala 6
outcomes.quote: BOLD response and DELTA power were negatively correlated during presentation of video sequence (correlation of BOLDDELTA time-courses r 1⁄4 �0.48 p < 0.01), while BOLD and HGP were positively correlated (correlation BOLD-HGP Spearman’s r 1⁄4 0.41 p < 0.01)
outcomes.notes: Needs the BOLD time course of the amygdala from the clinical fMRI (Methods 4.6, 4.10). The paper names no deposit of it; the dandiset holds no fMRI, nor does the iEEG-BIDS version of the same data on OpenNeuro (ds003374, snapshot 1.1.1, which holds only ieeg folders), and the data descriptor lists only iEEG, spikes and electrode positions.

outcomes.statement: Spike sorting gave 50 putative neuron clusters from 9 amygdalae, of which 41 had a firing rate above 1 Hz and were analysed.
outcomes.quote: We identified 50 putative clusters of neurons (Niediek et al., 2016) from 9 amygdalae and included those with firing rate >1 Hz (N 1⁄4 41 neurons) in further analysis
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 42 units, 42 above 1 Hz over the epochs each was recorded in (reading a, given as measured) and 40 over the whole 442 s (reading b); both within 4.1 of 41. The 50 putative clusters cannot be tested, as only units above about 1 Hz were deposited. Units are in 8 amygdalae, not 9, so the third expected value fails. The measured value is the first expected value only. The units come from 5 patients (1, 2, 3, 4, 7), which matches the abstract's 5 participants, but not the amygdalae of Table 1, which lists MUA for patients 5 and 8 and none for 7. Their mean rate over the observed epochs is 4.65 +- 3.91 Hz (median 3.13), against the data descriptor's 1.66 +- 2.65 Hz; 31 units are above 2 Hz.
deviations: Epochs in which a unit has no spike at all are taken as not recorded (16 units of subject 7 after epoch 11, 4 units of subject 2 in epoch 1), as their rates elsewhere are 1 to 16 Hz.

outcomes.statement: All 41 neurons fire more during AVERSIVE than during NEUTRAL sequences (FRV 0.26 plus or minus 0.15).
outcomes.quote: All 41 clusters of neurons increased their firing rate during the AVERSIVE condition (Firing Rate Variation, FRV 1⁄4 0.26 �0.15)
outcomes.notes: Over the 24 s blocks and observed epochs 27 of 42 units have FRV > 0, mean 0.033 +- 0.690 Hz (Wilcoxon against 0, p = 0.50); over the 26 s trials, or with all epochs, 23 to 26 positive and means 0.007 to 0.032 Hz. By subject the mean FRV runs from -0.21 to 0.62 Hz. Relative to each unit's mean rate it is 0.061 +- 0.231 (a variant).
deviations: Observed epochs as in neuron-count; the variant with all epochs is shown.

outcomes.statement: The neurons' firing rose gradually and stayed enhanced throughout the AVERSIVE sequences, not as an immediate response at onset.
outcomes.quote: Contrary to our expectation of an immediate spiking onset, the neurons increased their firing gradually and sustained enhanced firing throughout the AVERSIVE video sequences
outcomes.notes: The population AVERSIVE minus NEUTRAL rate (100 ms bins, 1 s smoothing) is 0.310 Hz over 0 to 2 s and 0.018 Hz over 2 to 24 s, with its first peak at 0.15 s and 4 of the twelve 2 s bins negative. Neither reading of the criterion holds. It is -0.078 Hz over the baseline clip.

outcomes.statement: Across neurons, the correlation of firing rate with macro-electrode HGP does not differ between the AVERSIVE and NEUTRAL conditions.
outcomes.quote: Across all neurons, the covariation of neuronal firing with HGP was not significantly different between the two experimental conditions (Spearman’s r 1⁄4 0.17 ... �0.28 in AVERSIVE, 0.18 �0.18 in NEUTRAL; Wilcoxon paired test, p > 0.05)
outcomes.notes: The readings of the claims file disagree; the claimed absence holds in 4 of 6. Per block and averaged no time base finds a difference (p 0.72 to 0.83), nor does the 1 s time base over the blocks laid end to end (r = 0.085 +- 0.130 in AVERSIVE and 0.094 +- 0.124 in NEUTRAL, p = 0.54, given as measured). Over the blocks laid end to end on the 1.5 s and 15 s time bases, each block smoothed on its own, the test finds NEUTRAL higher (p = 0.012 and 0.023, median differences -0.087 and -0.131). Smoothing over the whole session first (the first revision's form, now a variant) gave p = 0.002 and 0.009. The means are within the stated spreads under every reading. Partially reproduced and not blocked, because the six readings are named by the claims file, so no method detail is left to choose; the test ran under each, and the claimed absence holds under some and fails under others, that is, it holds only in part. Unlike the criteria of fig1b-delta-decrease and fig1f-hgp-more-specific-than-delta, this criterion does not say to block when its readings disagree. The time base is still asked of the authors (methods_unavailable).
deviations: In the readings with the blocks laid end to end, each block is smoothed (or binned) on its own before concatenation, so no sample carries another block or a baseline clip.
HGP is the Methods 4.8 envelope without per-trial normalisation; a per-block Spearman r is unchanged by any per-trial normalisation.

outcomes.statement: Across neurons, the correlation of firing rate with microwire high gamma power (muHGP) is higher in the AVERSIVE than in the NEUTRAL condition.
outcomes.quote: the covariation of neuronal firing with μHGP was higher during AVERSIVE than during NEUTRAL conditions (Spearman’s r 1⁄4 0.51 �0.18 during AVERSIVE, 0.43 �0.16 during NEUTRAL; Wilcoxon paired test, p < 0.01)
outcomes.notes: Needs the continuous microwire signals. The dandiset holds only spike times and mean waveforms of the microwire data, as the data descriptor says was shared; the OpenNeuro version holds macro iEEG only.

outcomes.statement: Across neurons, the spatial synchronization index (SSI) is strongly positively correlated with the firing rate variability (FRV).
outcomes.quote: We found a strong positive correlation across all participants between the SSI and FRV (Spearman’s r 1⁄4 0.78, p < 1e-7)
outcomes.notes: Over the 41 units with another unit in their amygdala, Spearman r between SSI and FRV is 0.26 (p = 0.11) on the 1 s time base and 0.40 (p = 0.009) on the 15 s one, against 0.78 with p < 1e-7. Neither reading gives the value, and the 1 s reading misses p < 0.05, so the partial result of the criterion does not hold either. Dropping the 4 pairs likely on one wire gives 0.24 (p = 0.13) and 0.35 (p = 0.023).
deviations: SSI uses every other unit of the same amygdala. Methods 4.11 say "on different microwires"; the units table has no microwire column (columns offset, spike_times, obs_intervals, electrodes, electrode_group, waveform_mean, waveform_sd), each unit points only to the bipolar macro channel, and the file holds one electrode group. So the Results' definition, "all neighboring neurons", is assumed. A variant drops pairs likely on one wire by a spike train test (no spikes within 1 ms of each other where the 2 to 12 ms flanks predict at least 3); it flags 4 of 116 testable pairs, and the others fire within 1 ms as often as the flanks predict (median ratio 1.19).

outcomes.statement: Across neurons, the ongoing firing rate correlates positively with muHGP (0.27), HGP (0.19) and BOLD (0.23), and the correlation is lowest with HGP.
outcomes.source: Results 2.3, paragraph 5; Figure 3D and its inset
outcomes.quote: Across all neurons and participants, the ongoing firing rate positively correlated with μHGP (Spearman’s r 1⁄4 0.27 �0.15), HGP (Spearman’s r 1⁄4 0.19 � 0.17) and BOLD (Spearman’s r 1⁄4 0.23 �0.20) ... Across all recording modalities, the correlation of the firing rate and other measures was lowest with HGP (Wilcoxon’s paired test, p < 1e-2)

statistics.about: correlation with HGP against those with muHGP and with BOLD

outcomes.notes: The firing-HGP Spearman r is 0.136 +- 0.241 with 15 s smoothing (reading a, given as measured) and 0.139 +- 0.195 on the 1.5 s time base, positive in 29 and 32 of 42 units, within 0.19 +- 0.17. The muHGP and BOLD correlations and the two tests that HGP is lowest cannot be computed, as the microwire signals and the BOLD time courses are not available. The measured value is the HGP mean, the second expected value; the first and third cannot be measured.
deviations: Only the HGP part is tested.

outcomes.statement: The per-neuron correlation of firing rate with HGP is described by both FRV and SSI in a multiple linear regression.
outcomes.quote: We found that the co-modulation between neuronal firing and HGP is described by both FVR and SSI (Fig. 4B, r 1⁄4 0.59, p < 1e-4)
outcomes.notes: With 15 s time bases for both the firing-HGP r and SSI, R = 0.635 (within 0.059 of 0.59) and model p = 5.6e-5; over the four readings R = 0.56 to 0.68 and model p from 6e-6 to 7e-4. SSI has p <= 2e-4 in every reading; FRV has p 0.07 to 0.65, with a negative coefficient in three, so the regression is described by SSI alone and the claim's "both FRV and SSI", which the criterion requires, fails in every reading. The SSI variant without likely same-wire pairs gives the same.
deviations: SSI as assumed in fig3c-ssi-frv-correlation.

findings.statement: The BOLD time courses of the clinical fMRI, on which six of the paper's claims rest, are not public. The dandiset holds none, the OpenNeuro version (ds003374, 1.1.1) holds only iEEG, and the paper names no deposit.
The continuous microwire signals behind the microwire high gamma power (muHGP) are not in the dandiset, which holds only spike times and mean waveforms of the microwire data.
Each session is deposited twice, as `_ecephys.nwb` and `_ecephys+image.nwb`; the second adds a link to the video and holds identical iEEG, spikes and trials. The 18 NWB files hold 9 recordings.
The iEEG is stated in volts, but its values (standard deviation 15 to 101, up to 1546) are microvolts.

The trial table gives trial 1 as 0 to 26 s, including its 2 s baseline clip, and trials 2 to 17 as their 24 s blocks only (starting 2 s into each 26 s epoch). The iEEG timestamps run without a gap from 0 to 442 s, but the 17 epochs are not contiguous; the signal jumps at each boundary (median step 12 to 36 against 1.4 to 1.9 within epochs).

Every unit's obs_intervals cover all 17 epochs, but the 16 units of subject 7 have no spike after 286 s (epochs 12 to 17) and four units of subject 2 none in epoch 1, at rates of 1 to 16 Hz elsewhere.

The ages of subjects 2 and 8 (39 and 24) differ from those in the paper and the data descriptor (48 and 27). Subject 2's file holds the same subject metadata as subject 7's (age 39, gliosis, AL and AR implanted, AR in the SOZ), the age being that of the paper's patient 7.

The electrode location of the right channel of subjects 1, 5 and 9 is "Right Hippocampus, rostral hippocampus", and both channels of subject 6 are "unknown", while their labels (AR, AL), the paper and the data descriptor place them in the amygdala.

Units are assigned only to the bipolar macro channel of their amygdala; the microwire each was recorded on is not given, so the paper's spatial synchronisation index (neurons on different microwires) cannot be computed as defined. The units table has no column for it, and a spike train test of coincident firing flags only 4 of 116 testable pairs as likely sharing a wire.

The units are in 8 amygdalae of 5 patients (1 L and R, 2 L and R, 3 L, 4 L, 7 L and R). The paper's Results give 9 amygdalae, and its Table 1 lists multi-unit activity for patients 5 and 8 and none for 7. Three of the 8 (1 R, 2 R, 7 R, with 17 units) are SOZ amygdalae, while the paper's Discussion 3.4 says there were no microwire recordings from SOZ amygdalae. Their mean rate is 4.65 +- 3.91 Hz against the data descriptor's 1.66 +- 2.65 Hz, and two units of subject 7 are below 1 Hz over the whole session.

Question for the authors. How were the power envelopes "z-scored within each trial" (Methods 4.8), over the whole 26 s trial, against the baseline clip, or otherwise? A z-score over the whole trial makes the baseline correction void and removes the sustained delta decrease, and with it every delta effect here; a z-score against the baseline keeps it. The outcome of fig1b-delta-decrease is blocked on this. Methods 4.8 also says results were quantitatively similar with the mean of all epochs or of the previous epoch as baseline; here the HGP clusters that begin in the first 2 s (nSOZ amygdalae) come only with these baselines, the previous epoch with z-scoring over the amygdala (0.6 to 5.5 s) and, with the trialsd variant, the mean of all epochs (0.6 to 1.9 s) and the previous epoch (0.5 to 8.4 s); the 1 s baseline clip gives none.

Question for the authors. Over which window was the modulation index of each amygdala computed? With these data the group test finds no HGP cluster, and per-amygdala tests find clusters in 1 to 3 of 14 amygdalae, while Table 2 prints an MI for every amygdala; the claims on the HGP MI rest on fixed windows (0 to 2 s for HGP, the whole block for delta) taken from the Results' text, an assumption, and the only failing reading of table2-delta-reduced-12-of-14 uses them.

Question for the authors. On what time base, and over which span (the condition's blocks laid end to end, or per block), were the per-neuron correlations of firing with HGP in Fig. 3B computed? The test finds no condition difference per block or on the 1 s time base, and finds NEUTRAL higher on the 1.5 s and 15 s time bases over blocks laid end to end.

Run on the paper's printed Table 2 values, the tests of Fig. 1E find the DELTA MI also different between nSOZ and SOZ amygdalae (rank-sum p = 0.035, t-test p = 0.013), against "HGP but not DELTA distinguishes"; the chi-square test of the printed counts 5/5 and 1/5 of Fig. 1F gives p = 0.0098 (0.053 with Yates' correction), not about 0.2; and the exact binomial interval for 7/7 is 59-100%, not the printed 66-100%, and no single binomial interval method gives all three printed intervals.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the archive's asset list and metadata for the blocked claims and tested the helper functions on synthetic inputs. It gave its own outcome for each of the 25 claims; 20 agree with the record of that round.

disagreements.reason: 11-13 negative, with negative values both inside and outside the SOZ, under window (a) wherever it is defined and under (c) except trial z-scoring (10). It fails under every per-amygdala window (b) reading (0-2 negative; most MIs are set to 0). The criterion requires every reading.

Under the claims file's MI windows, HGP is never more specific: (a) is undefined and (b) gives ties or reverses. Under the notebook's added window (c), HGP is more specific for 3 of 4 z-scorings. The chi-square p (0.001-0.11) never approaches the paper's ~0.2.

No difference at the Fig. 3A time base (both spans, p 0.37/0.83) or with any per-block span. The means are within the stated spreads. With 1.5 s and 15 s concatenated series, NEUTRAL > AVERSIVE at p=0.002 and 0.009.
R is within tolerance in 3 of 4 readings, but the FRV coefficient never reaches p<0.05 (0.07-0.65). The model p<1e-4 in only 2 of 4 readings.

entries.name: 000576-fedele-2020
entries.title: iEEG, neurons and BOLD in the human amygdala during aversive videos (Fedele, Tzovara et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Fedele, Tzovara et al. (2020) on dandiset 000576, which holds the bipolar amygdala iEEG of 9 patients (14 amygdalae) and the spike times of 42 units from 5 of them during a block design of aversive and neutral videos. It tests the delta and high gamma responses, the modulation indices and their relation to the seizure onset zone, and the firing of the units. The BOLD time courses and the continuous microwire signals are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Fedele, Tzovara et al. (2020) from dandiset 000576
